logline: A delinquent teenager inherits the powers of a Soul Reaper and discovers that the war between the living and the dead is more politically complex than any single hero can resolve - a classic shonen that found its greatest achievement twenty years into its run.

renewal.note: The original series ran 2004-2012 (366 eps). The Thousand-Year Blood War arc aired 2022-2024 in four cours across Crunchyroll and Disney+, concluding the manga's story. No sequel announced.

bollymeter.basis: The Soul Society arc (eps 1-63) established Bleach's reputation with one of shonen's most celebrated rescues-as-espionage storylines. The aesthetic design - particularly the Shinigami court hierarchy - attracted strong critical praise, even as the filler problem that would define the series' middle period began to emerge.

seasons.review_body: The original series began in 2004 as one of Shonen Jump's 'Big Three' alongside Naruto and One Piece. The first major arc - Ichigo's assault on Soul Society to rescue Rukia - is the franchise's creative peak for the original run. Director Noriyuki Abe and Studio Pierrot constructed the Soul Society as a genuine political institution with factions, hierarchies, and internal conflicts, a complexity that gave the rescue narrative more texture than the premise suggested. Episodes 1-63 carry a clarity of purpose that the series' prolonged filler periods gradually diluted. The Rukia rescue arc remains the original series' most consistently praised material, cited in retrospective reviews as a defining shonen arc of the 2000s.

episode_reviews.title: The Day I Became a Shinigami
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere establishes Ichigo as a protagonist with an unusual emotional baseline: he sees ghosts and treats that fact with weary pragmatism rather than horror. The introduction of Rukia - authoritative, businesslike, briefly human - and the Soul Reaper transfer sequence efficiently sets the series' mechanical premise.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Ichigo accepting Rukia's powers to save his family - the handover that defines the next 400 episodes - lands as an act of desperation rather than heroism, which is the right register.

bollymeter.basis: The Arrancar and Hueco Mundo arcs contain genuinely excellent material - the Espada designs, Aizen as antagonist - diluted by what became the series' central critical failure: extensive filler episodes that broke narrative momentum. Retrospective reviews acknowledge the arc's highs while noting the structural damage.

seasons.review_body: The Arrancar arc through to the Fake Karakura Town battle (eps 64-310) represents the original series' longest and most contentious stretch. The introduction of Aizen as a long-game antagonist whose plan had been operational since the beginning was the arc's structural strength; the Espada as a collection of conceptually interesting villains was a design triumph. But the filler ratio across this section - estimated by fan archives at over 30 percent of episodes - inflicted lasting reputational damage. The Hueco Mundo arc in particular saw the main plot stall for extended periods. The retrospective consensus identifies this stretch as the reason the original series' reputation eroded despite its creative ambitions.
seasons.season_over_season: The Arrancar era contains the series' most ambitious villain design but its most severe pacing failures - the filler problem that would define the original run's legacy begins here.

bollymeter.basis: The Fullbring arc (eps 343-366) is the original series' weakest stretch - a power reset that critics found uninspired, concluding a run that had been in decline since the Arrancar era's filler saturation.

seasons.review_body: The Fullbring arc (2012) closed the original series with a storyline that landed as anticlimactic. Ichigo's power loss and reacquisition via a new group of characters introduced late in the run read as a missed opportunity to bring the Aizen storyline to a more resonant conclusion. The original series ended in March 2012 after 366 episodes, with the manga's final arc - the Thousand-Year Blood War - unacknowledged by the adaptation. The ending generated significant fan dissatisfaction, which made the 2022 announcement of a TYBW adaptation a major cultural event in anime communities.
seasons.season_over_season: The Fullbring arc is a structural and creative decline from every standard the series had previously set - the original run ended without its best chapter.

bollymeter.basis: The Thousand-Year Blood War arc aired 2022-2024 and received near-unanimous critical acclaim as a franchise redemption. Pierrot's upgraded animation - Disney+ co-production budget - and the Quincy mythology delivered what reviewers called the best arc in the series' history. Rotten Tomatoes tracked audience approval above 95 percent.

pull_quotes.text: Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War is a triumphant return, easily the best arc in the series' nearly 20-year history.

seasons.review_body: The Thousand-Year Blood War arc (2022-2024) is one of anime's most discussed franchise revivals. Ten years after the original series ended without adapting its best material, Pierrot returned with a co-production budget that produced animation critics described as a different category from the original run. The Quincy antagonists - Yhwach and the Sternritter - provided a mythology of genuine depth, recontextualising the entire original series' conflict. Multiple Bankai reveals that the manga had saved for this arc landed as major fan events. Anime News Network and IGN both cited the TYBW adaptation as among the best anime of 2022-2024. The arc's reception confirmed what manga readers had argued for years: Bleach's original run underserved its own peak material.
seasons.season_over_season: The Thousand-Year Blood War is not merely better than the original run's later arcs - it operates at a different level entirely, and the franchise's legacy is now measured from here.

episode_reviews.title: The Blood Warfare
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The TYBW premiere announces its ambitions in the first five minutes: the animation quality, score, and pacing all signal that this is a different production than the one that ended in 2012. The premiere functions as both a reintroduction for lapsed viewers and a reward for those who read the manga.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The Wandenreich invasion sequence - an army materialising in Soul Society without warning - lands as the franchise's most effective threat introduction.

critic_note.text: Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War is a triumphant return, easily the best arc in the series' nearly 20-year history.

episode_reviews.title: The End
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The climax of Part 1 delivers multiple Bankai reveals that the franchise had been withholding for years, each animated with a care that made the reveals genuine events. This single episode justified the ten-year wait for the adaptation.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Zaraki Kenpachi's instinctive Bankai - a sequence that Studio Pierrot animated with extraordinary deliberateness - became one of the most discussed anime moments of 2023.
